title: The Pledge of Divine Pleasure (Bay'at al-Ridwan)
subtitle: Beneath the Samurah Tree: Unconditional Devotion unto Death
summary: The diplomatic parleys at Hudaybiyyah, Urwah ibn Mas'ud's awe before Quraysh, Uthman's mission into Makkah, the false report of his murder, the solemn pledge of fourteen hundred companions beneath the Samurah tree, and the descent of divine Sakinah.

sections.text: While encamped at Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ initiated intensive diplomatic contacts to convince the Makkan leadership that the Muslims had come solely to perform the rites of Umrah and venerate the Sacred House. A succession of Makkan envoys arrived at the Muslim camp: Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i, Mikraz ibn Hafs, and Hulays ibn Alqamah, the chieftain of the Ahabish desert confederates. When Hulays saw the seventy sacrificial camels garlanded with cords and emaciated from travel, he was moved to tears and returned to Makkah rebuking Quraysh: 'By Allah, it is not just that these consecrated animals be turned away from the sanctuary!'

Quraysh then dispatched Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi, a seasoned aristocrat of Ta'if. Urwah observed the Muslim camp with acute scrutiny. Returning to Makkah, he addressed the assembly of Quraysh in awe: 'O people! By Allah, I have visited the emperors of the earth; I have stood before Caesar of Rome, Chosroes of Persia, and the Negus of Abyssinia, yet by Allah, never have I seen any monarch whose subjects revere him as the companions of Muhammad revere Muhammad! When he speaks, they lower their voices in his presence, and none among them gazes directly into his eyes out of immense respect. He has offered you a reasonable plan of peace, so accept it!'
The Mission of Uthman & The False Report

To deliver a direct, personal letter to the aristocratic elders of Quraysh, the Prophet ﷺ selected Uthman ibn Affan, whose powerful Umayyad lineage provided diplomatic immunity within Makkah. Uthman entered Makkah under the protection of his kinsman Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-Aas. He conveyed the Prophet's peaceful intentions and visited the secret, oppressed believers trapped in Makkah, comforting them with glad tidings of imminent liberation. Quraysh offered Uthman permission to perform Tawaf around the Ka'bah alone, but he refused with noble loyalty: 'I shall never circumambulate the House until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ does so first!'

Quraysh detained Uthman in prolonged negotiations. As days passed without word, a persistent rumor swept through the camp at Hudaybiyyah that Uthman had been assassinated inside the city. The killing of an official diplomatic emissary was regarded across ancient Arabia as an unforgivable declaration of total war.
Beneath the Samurah Tree: Bay'at al-Ridwan

Upon hearing the report, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned the entire army, declaring: 'We shall not depart until we fight the people!' He sat beneath the sprawling shade of an ancient thorny acacia (Samurah) tree. One by one, fourteen hundred companions stepped forward, placing their hands into the hand of the Prophet ﷺ and pledging an unconditional oath (Bay'ah): pledging steadfastness unto death, swearing never to flee the battlefield, and offering their lives for the cause of God.

When all had pledged, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took his own left hand and placed it firmly over his right hand, declaring: 'And this hand is for Uthman!' Through that sublime gesture, the Prophet took the pledge on behalf of his absent diplomat, elevating Uthman's honor above all present.

۞ لَّقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَابَهُمْ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا
'Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.' (Surah Al-Fath 48:18)

Muslim 1856 and Muslim 1858 say they were fourteen hundred at the tree, and that they pledged not to flee, not to fight to the death. Muslim 1857 gives thirteen hundred. The reports do not say that no one who pledged would enter the Fire. What the Quran says is that Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged under the tree (48:18). The sirah then says that news came of Uthman being alive, and that Quraysh sent a negotiator.

references.title: The Holy Quran
references.author: Surah Al-Fath (48:10 & 48:18)
references.notes: Divine testimony to the Pledge of Ridwan beneath the tree and the descent of tranquility.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.source: Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Ghazwat al-Hudaybiyyah, Hadith 4153–4169
references.notes: The Hudaybiyyah material in Bukhari's Book of Maghazi includes Urwah and the pledge. The span 4153–4169 was not re-opened number by number, so it is not asserted as a block.

references.title: Sahih Muslim
references.author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 261 AH)
references.notes: 1856 and 1858: fourteen hundred, the pledge not to flee. 1857: thirteen hundred. None of these three says that they would not enter the Fire. That sentence has been removed.
